title: In seven CMIP6 atmosphere models, the 1979-2014 radiation response to AMIPII-minus-HadISST2 SST differences is 1.2-4 times the Green's-function prediction, so GF artifact biases are probably too small
abstract: Question: earlier campaign studies calculated how SST forcing artifacts (the 1981 HadISST1-to-OI v2 splice in AMIPII, OI v2 and sea-ice steps) change radiative feedback with linear Green's functions (GFs), not with model runs. Do real atmosphere models respond to SST-dataset differences as the GFs predict? Approach: seven CMIP6 models ran both amip (PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.3 SST and sea ice) and HighResMIP highresSST-present (HadISST2.2) over 1979-2014. For each same-model pair (36 amip and 8 highresSST-present runs) we took dN = N(amip) - N(highresSST-present) and compared it with the GFMIP GF prediction (5-model mean of CAM5, CanESM5, ECHAM6, GFDL-AM4, HadAM3; also CAM4) from the SST difference the model saw, plus a CAM5 albedo-kernel sea-ice term. Results: the regression scaling of dN on the 5-GF prediction is 1.2 to 3.9 (median 1.9) for annual means with a cubic trend removed and 1.1 to 4.0 (median 2.4) without volcanic years; monthly 0.7 to 3.3 (median 1.5). It stays above 1 with the GF of the same model family (ECHAM6 for MPI-ESM1-2-HR 2.1-3.6; GFDL-AM4 1.4-1.8). A control regression of each run on its own full SST gives 0.0 to 1.2, so the excess is specific to the dataset-difference patterns. From 1985-1990 to 1994-2008 the 60S-60N mean SST difference does not change, but the pattern does (AMIP tropics 0.1 K colder, 40-60S 0.25 K warmer); dN rises by +0.17 to +0.92 W m-2 in all seven pairs (median +0.46) against +0.15 predicted (median ratio 3.3). Pooled regional sensitivities: warm pool -15.8 +/- 3.0 W m-2 per K (GF -9.3) and 40-60S +5.9 +/- 1.5 (GF -0.4). The 1981 splice step in dN is -0.23 +/- 0.12 W m-2 (-0.37 without El Chichon months) against -0.16 to -0.21 predicted, so 1.5-1.7 times but not decisive. The 2009 Antarctic sea-ice step matches the kernel term. In four pairs without clear-sky trend differences, the dataset choice changes the 1979-2014 trend of N by +0.03 to +0.11 W m-2 per decade, while the GFs predict about 0. Implication: GF-based artifact feedback biases are probably lower bounds in models like these. Limitations: the two experiment sets also differ in start year, daily versus monthly SST and, in three pairs, forcing (clear-sky differences); only two pairs have a same-family GF; single highresSST-present members dominate the noise; the study does not test which SST dataset is right.

display.caption: (top) Annual TOA net radiation difference N(amip) - N(highresSST-present): seven same-model pairs (grey), their mean (blue), and the prediction from the 5-GF mean plus the sea-ice kernel term (orange; band: CanESM5 to CAM4 GF). Dashed: the 1981-11 AMIP splice; dotted: the 2009 AMIP Antarctic sea-ice step; grey bands: volcanic periods. (bottom) 60S-60N mean SST difference AMIP minus HadISST2 as seen by the models.

(a) Scaling factor a in dN = a x (5-GF prediction) + b x (ice term) for each pair: monthly, annual with cubic trend removed, and annual without volcanic years; grey squares: control regression of each amip run on the GF prediction from its own SST. (b) a for each single GF (grey) and for the GF of the same model family (blue, 95% interval). a = 1 means the GF is right.

(a) Regional sensitivity of dN (global W m-2 per K of regional-mean SST difference): models pooled (blue, 95%), single pairs (grey) and the 5-GF mean and range (orange). (b) dN step at the 1981-11 AMIP splice: real (blue, 95%) and predicted (orange; bar: CanESM5 to CAM4). (c) Change of dN from 1985-1990 to 1994-2008, when the mean SST difference does not change: real versus predicted.
